versions.agent: Claude Code subagents, same session model in both arms
versions.harness: playwright-core 1.64.1, lighthouse 13.6.0 (mobile, simulated throttling, 3 runs, median), Chromium build 1194

install.command: copy SKILL.md into .claude/skills/performance-optimization/ (or claude plugin install from the addyosmani marketplace)

fixtures: fixtures/11-perf: task/ (SoundBench, a self-contained 24-headphone review page, deliberately slow: 2.98 MB unsized hero PNG, 300 KB synchronous analytics bundle whose tiny tq() the table render depends on, 400 ms busy-wait polyfill, 1.5 MB unread inline JSON, 4 TTF @font-faces without font-display, N+1 fetch of 24 product files, 236 KB CSS with 400 unused rules, late-inserted promo banner (CLS 0.23), unsized/unlazy below-fold PNGs; gen/gen.mjs regenerates it), hidden/ (functional.mjs 15 browser checks incl. tie-break sort, brand filter, compare cap 4, banner text; lighthouse.mjs; server.mjs), reference/ (1.0, LH 100, 35 KB), grade.mjs, KEY.md
design: Arm A = plain subagent told to make the page fast without breaking features; Arm B = same prompt + 'read fixtures/skills/performance-optimization.SKILL.md first and follow it'. 3 reps per arm, fresh copies. Score = 0.5 × functional (15 checks) + 0.5 × clamp((LH − 17)/(95 − 17)). Untouched task 0.5 (LH 17). Pilot (plain agent) scored 1.0 (LH 100) so the trial sits at the ceiling; it was not hardened further because the slowness is already eight interacting causes with a cross-file trap (removing the analytics bundle breaks the table) and the brief's time box was spent. Secondary metrics kept per run: LH score, LCP, CLS, TBT, transferred bytes. Four of the six arm runs (A-1, B-1, B-2, B-3) were interrupted by an API rate limit and resumed; their usage rows cover the resumed segment only.

candidate_default.config: Arm B with the performance-optimization skill
candidate_default.observed: All six runs kept 15/15 features (every run kept a tq() stub or queue, none fell into the analytics trap) and reached LH ≥ 96. Arm B followed the skill visibly: each run measured before and after every change with the README's Lighthouse command and left a PERF.md ledger; B-3 reverted a font-fallback change its own measurement showed made CLS worse. Arm B left the 1.47 MB TTF fonts in place in all three runs (1.81-1.83 MB transferred) because WOFF2 subsetting tooling is absent on this machine; two of three plain runs dropped or replaced the webfont instead (350-387 KB). Tool-call and wall-time means for arm B are post-resume segments and are not comparable to arm A.

candidate_tuned.note: not run; the skill has no knobs

limits: Ceiling: 6/6 runs at 1.0; the score cannot separate the arms. The secondary metrics (bytes, LCP) favour arm A on page weight, but by one design choice (fonts), not by method.

Usage: 4 of 6 runs resumed after a rate limit, so tokens are inflated for both arms (double context) and tool calls/seconds for arm B are truncated; only the direction of the token delta (+13 %) is meaningful.
n = 3 per arm; Lighthouse is run 3 times per grade with the median taken (all medians equal to all three runs here).
verdict: REJECT as a default (ceiling, no measurable gain, +13 % tokens); WATCH for the measure-first ledger (PERF.md) if the Owner wants auditable performance work
reason: Both arms hit 1.0 in every rep: the plain agent already finds all eight seeded causes and avoids the cross-file trap. The skill's only visible effect is process (per-change measurement and a written ledger), which costs tokens and did not change the outcome; it also made the agent more conservative (fonts kept, 1.8 MB pages vs 0.35-0.39 MB for two plain runs).
do_not_adopt_notes: Do not adopt as a default for page-speed fixes; the plain agent is at the ceiling on this task size.
